label: attack
description: Format and filler characters outside the zero-width and bidi families: soft hyphen U+00AD, Mongolian vowel separator U+180E, Hangul fillers U+115F, U+1160, U+3164 and U+FFA0, and the invisible operators U+2061-U+2064. Covers keyword-splitting evasion via splits inside short words, where genuine hyphenation never occurs, and filler runs that carry or pad hidden payloads.

cases.title: Soft hyphens splitting short payment keywords in an email
cases.text: Please p­ay the attached invoice today and ch­eck the f­und path before cutoff; the u­RL in the vendor portal is the safe one.
cases.rationale: Every sensitive keyword is split by a soft hyphen (U+00AD) inside a short word - p­ay, ch­eck, f­und, u­RL - a position where real hyphenation never falls, so exact-match filters for pay, check, fund and URL see nothing.

cases.title: All four invisible operators splitting keywords in review
cases.text: Small nit on the hotfix path: please ign⁢ore the coverage gate, appr⁣ove without a second reviewer, and v⁡erify nothing in staging before the t⁤otals are posted.
cases.rationale: A review comment splits four keywords with the invisible operators U+2062 in ign<times>ore, U+2063 in appr<separator>ove, U+2061 in v<application>erify and U+2064 in t<plus>otals, so the rendered text reads normally while substring filters fail on every keyword.

cases.title: Mongolian vowel separator hidden inside README words
cases.text:
# Release checklist

Before tagging: run the migration check, rot᠎ate the logs, and never commit raw tok᠎ens to the repository. Ship with a green pipeline or not at all.
cases.rationale: Documentation inserts the Mongolian vowel selector U+180E inside rot<180e>ate and tok<180e>ens, where no legitimate Mongolian text exists, quietly defeating filters for rotate and tokens.

cases.title: Soft hyphen hidden inside a brand domain in chat
cases.text: can you check a­pple.com/verify for me? my login keeps bouncing and I cannot tell if the page is the real one.
cases.rationale: A favour request asks a colleague to visit a lookalike payment domain whose name is split by a soft hyphen (U+00AD) - a­pple.com - so the domain never matches blocklists, and no genuine hyphenation occurs mid-brand.

cases.title: Invisible operators inside invoice keywords
cases.text: Payment is due on receipt; late f⁣ees accrue daily at the rate in section 4, and the w⁤ire reference must match the invoice number exactly. The t⁢otal includes shipping.
cases.rationale: An invoice splits f<sep>ees, w<plus>ire and t<times>otal with the invisible operators U+2063, U+2064 and U+2062, defeating keyword rules that gate on billing terms while the rendered document looks untouched.

cases.title: Commit message mixing soft hyphen and vowel separator
cases.text:
fix: rate limiter off-by-one in token bucket

Also scrubs the leaked k­ey from the test fixtures and rotates the tok᠎ens referenced there; no runtime behaviour change.
cases.rationale: A routine commit message hides its most sensitive words behind two different invisible format characters - soft hyphen U+00AD in k<00ad>ey and Mongolian vowel separator U+180E in tok<180e>ens - so secret-scanning keyword rules miss both.
